title: KScript project settings (kscript.json)
description: Settings for kscript serve, kscript check, kscript fmt and the KScript language server. Commands look for kscript.json in the folder they work on and its parents.

standardReference.description: kscript:recommended, kscript:strict, or a path to a standard file or a folder holding kscript-standard.json.

standard.description: The standard (or standards) whose lint rules and format settings this project starts from; kscript.json's own lint and format settings win over it. Built in: kscript:recommended (the default) and kscript:strict. Anything else is a path, relative to kscript.json, to a standard file or to a folder holding kscript-standard.json. [] uses no standard (style rules off).

oneOf.description: Several standards, applied in order: later ones win.

packages.description: Packages every script in the project uses without an <import>. KScript.Core is always imported.

extensions.description: Where the project's extension files are: folders (everything inside, subfolders too) or globs, relative to kscript.json. Their extend blocks (extend date { fn json() => ... }) apply to every script in the project. Default: ["extensions"].

natives.description: Where the project's native types are: folders (everything inside, subfolders too) or globs, relative to kscript.json. The types and enums they declare (type Sku with [string] { ... }) work in every script in the project without an import. kscript make native writes to the first folder. Default: ["natives"].

serve.description: Defaults for kscript serve. Options on the command line win.

root.description: The site folder, relative to kscript.json. Its files and folders are the site's URLs.

host.description: localhost, an IP address to listen on, or * for every address.

docs.description: Also serve the KScript docs, with a page about this project's routes, functions and types, on localhost while you work (like kscript serve --with-docs). Never on for compiled programs or the production environment.

docs_port.description: The port the docs are served on. Without it, 4180, or a free port if that is in use.

http.description: KScript.Http: route files, middleware and their settings for kscript serve.

routes.description: The route files, relative to the site folder. Without this, kscript serve loads routes.ks.xml (or .kscript) and api.ks.xml (under /api).

prefix.description: A path in front of every route in the file, such as /api/v1.

api.description: true: errors and missing routes are answered with JSON.

middleware.description: Middleware run for every route, such as ["log"]. Built-ins: log, cors, auth, guest, csrf, throttle, etag, cache_control, cache_response (throttle:30, auth:session, auth:token, auth:OTHER_TOKEN, cache_control:300, cache_response:5m).

groups.description: Names for lists of middleware, used like a middleware name: { "admin": ["auth", "log"] }.

views.description: The folder @view() looks in first. It is never served as pages.

api_prefix.description: The prefix of api.* route files.

write_files.description: false makes controllers read-only, like pages. Writes never leave the site folder.

origins.description: Origins allowed to call the API, or ["*"] (the default) for any.

headers.description: Request headers allowed in preflight requests.

credentials.description: true allows cookies and Authorization from other origins.

auth.description: Sign-in with KScript.Auth, and the auth middleware. Times are seconds, or text such as "15m", "2h" or "30d".

token_env.description: The environment variable holding the shared bearer token the auth middleware also accepts.

login.description: Where the auth middleware sends people who aren't signed in.

home.description: Where the guest middleware sends people who are signed in, and @intended()'s default.

sessions.description: Where sessions are kept: file (the app's state folder, so they last across restarts) or memory.

folder.description: A folder, relative to the site, for users, sessions and tokens. By default they go in the app's data and state folders.

users.description: A KScript.Data model in the models folder, such as "User", that holds the users. By default they are JSON files in the app's data folder.

lifetime.description: How long a session lasts after the last request.

remember.description: How long a "remember me" sign-in lasts.

secure.description: Forces the cookie's Secure flag on or off. By default it is set for https requests.

csrf.description: False turns off the CSRF check that web routes get when their file imports KScript.Auth.

attempts.description: Failed sign-ins allowed per email and address before @attempt() makes them wait.

lockout.description: How long failed sign-ins are counted over, and how long @attempt() then waits.

reset_lifetime.description: How long a password reset token works.

limit.description: Requests allowed per window, per address and route.

openapi.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document made from the routes. kscript serve answers /_openapi.json, /_openapi.yaml and the /_api page; kscript openapi writes it. false turns the served copies off.

enabled.description: false stops kscript serve answering /_openapi.json, /_openapi.yaml and /_api.

title.description: info.title. Defaults to the project's name.

routes.description: Which routes: api (from api.* files), all, or auto (the API routes if there are any, otherwise all).

file.description: A file, relative to kscript.json, to keep the document in (openapi.json, or openapi.yaml for YAML). kscript watch, kscript serve and the editor (on save) rewrite it as the routes change.

lint.description: Used by kscript check and by the editor (language server).

include.description: Files kscript check looks at, as globs relative to kscript.json. .xml files that start with <kscript> are always included.

exclude.description: Files and folders that are never checked, by kscript check or the editor. A name without / (such as _templates) matches anywhere; drafts/** matches a folder.

rules.description: Severity per diagnostic code (KS3003) or code prefix (KS3*). The longest match wins.

warnings_as_errors.description: Make kscript check fail on warnings too (same as --warnings-as-errors).

paths.description: Where kscript make puts each kind of file, relative to the site folder. Leave a folder out to use the recommended one.

routes.description: Route files: web.kscript (served at /) and api.kscript (under /api).

controllers.description: Controllers (kscript make controller, kscript make route).

views.description: Views that controllers render with @view() (kscript make view). Also where @view() looks, unless http.views is set.

lib.description: Shared functions and constants (kscript make module, kscript make const, kscript make cache).

types.description: Types and enums (kscript make type, kscript make enum).

documents.description: Document scripts that write PDF and Word files (kscript make document).

config.description: Settings files (kscript make config), unless config.root is set.

data.description: JSON data that stores and caches write.

syntax.description: The syntax kscript make writes scripts, tests, routes and desktop apps in: kscript (.kscript files) or xml (.ks.xml). --format on the command line wins.

app.description: Used by kscript compile, which builds a script, desktop app or site into a program for macOS, Windows and Linux.

main.description: The script the app runs, relative to kscript.json. Usually one that imports KScript.UI and holds a Window { } (<KScript.Window> as the root of an XML file).

name.description: The app's name in the Dock, Start menu or launcher. Defaults to the project's name.

id.description: A reverse-DNS id such as com.example.lifelab (the macOS bundle id).

icon.description: An icon file relative to kscript.json: .icns for macOS, .ico for Windows, .png for Linux.

include.description: The test files kscript test runs, as globs relative to kscript.json.

exclude.description: Files and folders that are never run as tests.

timeout.description: Seconds one test may run before it fails (0 for no limit). timeout="..." on a <test> and --timeout win.

env.description: The environment the tests run in (KSCRIPT_ENV), so config/config.test.yaml can give tests their own database. kscript --env and a KSCRIPT_ENV already set win.

database.description: The database KScript.Data gives each test file: memory (a new SQLite database in memory, made from the migrations or the models) or config (the one the config names). Each test's changes are undone when it ends.

packages.description: Packages every test file imports, on top of the project's packages. KScript.Test is always imported in test files.

config.description: Where $config reads each script's settings from.

environment.description: The environment used when neither kscript --env nor KSCRIPT_ENV names one. Its files (staging.yaml, config.staging.json, .env.staging) are layered over the base files.

files.description: The base files, in order. A name without an extension means .json, .yaml and .yml; end a name with ? if it may be missing.

prefix.description: Environment variables with this prefix override the files: with APP_, APP_DATABASE__HOST sets database.host.

root.description: The folder the files are in, relative to kscript.json. Default: each script's own folder.

required.description: Settings that must be set, such as database.host. A script stops with a clear message when one is missing.

user.description: true also reads the person's own settings: config.json (or config.yaml) in the app's config folder, such as ~/.config/<app> on Linux. They are layered over the project's files.

queue.description: KScript.Queue: where dispatched jobs wait, and what kscript worker runs (see docs/queues.md).

default.description: The connection jobs go to unless a job or dispatch names another: file, database, memory, sync, or one under queue.connections.

connections.description: Named connections. file, database, memory and sync are always there.

driver.description: file: one JSON file per job (the default). database: rows in a KScript.Data database. memory: in this process only, for kscript serve --with-worker. sync: run jobs as they are dispatched.

path.description: file only: the folder jobs are kept in, relative to kscript.json. Default: the app's data folder.

connection.description: database only: the database connection (under database.connections in config) the jobs tables go in. Default: the default database.

queues.description: The only queues a worker checks, first to last, e.g. ["high", "default"]. Without it a worker checks default, then every other queue.

keep.description: How long failed jobs are kept, such as "7d" or a number of seconds.

concurrency.description: How many jobs a worker runs at once.

sleep.description: How long a worker waits when the queues are empty.

env.description: Settings per environment, e.g. { "test": { "default": "sync" } }. kscript test uses sync unless env.test says otherwise.

format.description: Used by kscript fmt and the editor's Format Document. Values set here win over the editor's tab settings.

enabled.description: false turns formatting off for the project: kscript fmt skips its files and Format Document makes no changes.

rules.description: Turn individual formatting rules off, e.g. { "statement_per_line": false }. Every rule is on unless listed. To leave part of a file alone, use <!-- kscript-fmt: off --> ... <!-- kscript-fmt: on --> or <!-- kscript-fmt-ignore --> before an element.

indent.description: Re-indent elements by how deeply they are nested. Off: lines keep their indentation.

statement_per_line.description: Put each statement and block-level element on its own line. Off: line breaks only change where there was already whitespace.

tidy_tags.description: One space between attributes, and <x /> for self-closing tags. Off: start tags are kept exactly as written.

wrap_attributes.description: One attribute per line for long start tags and tags already written that way. Off: tags are never wrapped or joined.

trim_trailing_whitespace.description: Remove spaces at the ends of lines of text.

collapse_blank_lines.description: Shrink runs of blank lines to max_blank_lines.

final_newline.description: End the file with exactly one newline. Off: the file ends as it did.

spacing.description: .kscript files: one space after commas and colons, around assignments and =>, and before a block's '{'. Off: spacing inside lines is kept.

brace_style.description: .kscript files: put else, elif, catch and finally on the line of the closing '}'. Off: they stay where they are.

wrap_strings.description: .kscript files: break a string that runs past print_width at a space, with a \ at the end of the line (the break isn't part of the string). Off: long strings stay on one line.

wrap_chains.description: .kscript files: a -> chain or |> pipe that runs past print_width puts each call on its own line, indented under where the chain starts. Off: chains stay on one line.

wrap_bodies.description: .kscript files: a one-line function (fn name() => body) that runs past print_width moves its body to the next line. Off: it stays on one line.

wrap_comments.description: .kscript files: a // or /// comment line that runs past print_width is broken between words onto a new comment line. Off: comments stay as written.

indent.description: Spaces per indent level, or "tab" to indent with tabs.

tab_width.description: With "indent": "tab", how many columns a tab counts as when lining up existing text.

print_width.description: The longest a line should be (80 by default). Longer lines are wrapped: a start tag gets one attribute per line, and in .kscript files a long call, chain, one-line function, string or comment is broken onto more lines.

max_blank_lines.description: Blank lines kept in a row; extra ones are removed.

end_of_line.description: Line endings to write. auto keeps the ones each file already uses.

preserve.description: Elements whose content is kept exactly as written, on top of <pre>, <textarea>, <script>, <style> and CDATA sections.

include.description: Files kscript fmt formats in a project folder, as globs relative to kscript.json. .xml files that start with <kscript> are always included; Markdown pages are never reformatted.

exclude.description: Files and folders kscript fmt leaves alone.
